Prim

prim · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Prim is stiffly formal, precise, and proper, often to the point of prudishness.

The prim librarian sniffed disapprovingly at the students' whispered conversation.

Worked Example

With her hands folded neatly in her lap and her ankles crossed just so, the prim contestant looked deeply uncomfortable when the host cracked a crude joke.

Prim goes beyond simple politeness -- it suggests someone who is fussy, easily scandalized, and strictly observant of proper manners.

How Strong Is It? — proper → prim → prissy

proper vs. prim

proper vs. prim: Proper simply means following good manners, without prim's extra note of easily-offended fussiness.

prissy vs. prim

prissy vs. prim: Prissy pushes prim's fussiness even further, into an exaggerated, easily-scandalized primness.

Put it together

Put it together: Prim is unusual among this unit's words -- it appeared in English in the 1700s from an origin etymologists still debate, with no confirmed Latin or Greek root to trace back further.

Word Building

Word Choice

Prim describes a stiff, fussy, almost prudish correctness -- more judgmental in tone than this unit's staid (a general seriousness) or sedate (a calm, unhurried pace); a prim person is often quick to disapprove of anything they see as improper.
